TomTom Traffic Index 2025 Analysis: London, New York, Tokyo Congestion Trends & Japan's Urban Traffic Crisis

📅 May 18, 2026 ✍️ Auto Prove Editorial Team 🏷️ TomTom, Traffic Index 2025, congestion, London, New York, Tokyo, Kumamoto, Kyoto, urban mobility, Area Analytics
🔗 Read the source article →

💡 Quick summary

TomTom's 2025 Traffic Index reveals rising congestion in Tokyo driven by return-to-office and tourism, congestion pricing showing results in New York, and Kumamoto emerging as Japan's most congested city due to TSMC semiconductor factory expansion.

📌 Key takeaways

  • TomTom analyzed 3.65 trillion km of driving data from connected cars, fleet operators, and smartphones across 500 global cities for its 15th annual Traffic Index.
  • London's congestion level rose 1 point year-over-year, peaking at 138% on September 10 with just 2.6 km traveled in 15 minutes.
  • New York's average travel time improved 1% thanks to Manhattan congestion pricing and bike lane infrastructure investments.
  • Tokyo's average congestion level rose 7.3% to 44.1%, driven by return-to-office trends and surging inbound tourism.
  • Kumamoto ranked #1 among 12 Japanese cities (56.7% congestion, 154 hours lost/year) due to TSMC's JASM subsidiary creating a surge in logistics and commuter traffic.
  • Kyoto recorded Japan's slowest average speed (17.5 km/h), ranking 8th slowest globally.
  • Japan's worst congestion day was Christmas (December 25), with March 21 (Kamakura, 106.8%) and August 8 also topping the charts.
  • TomTom's Area Analytics tool lets governments and businesses extract granular traffic data by region, date, and time for urban planning and location analysis.
